evidence.claim: 'Boring financial stocks' were green on the crash day and the crash week — named rotation destination

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Will Rising Long Term Rates Crash Stocks? (Sep 14)
evidence.claim: Banks and insurers outperform as long rates rise: net interest margin expands (DBS/OCBC/UOB, JPM), insurers reinvest float at higher yields (Arch Capital ACGL), ICE earns margin interest and rides rising energy-futures volume
evidence.relation: rising long rates → NIM and float-income expansion for financials

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Stock Market Insights. The Last 4 Months of 2026 (2026-09-03)
evidence.claim: The 10-year Treasury yield rose from 4.19% to 4.78% YTD, steepening the yield curve, and Khoo says banks are doing very well.
evidence.relation: A steeper curve lets banks borrow at short rates and lend at long rates, which expands net interest margin and earnings.

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Are the 3 Singapore Banks Cheap Enough? Buy DBS, UOB or OCBC? (2026-11-10)
evidence.claim: Khoo values all 3 Singapore banks via 5-yr average P/B and justified P/B (normalized ROE vs cost of equity): DBS fair range still far below market, OCBC above fair — after a 12-20% dip banks are NOT cheap enough to add; he holds but will not buy. Attractive headline yields lean on unfunded special dividends; ordinary-only yields sit close to govt bond yields.
evidence.relation: bank valuations stretched vs P/B fair value caps upside despite the rising-rate NIM tailwind

resolution: Two legs coexist: rate-tailwind evidence (NIM/float expansion, curve steepening) says banks earn more; the Nov-10 P/B valuation check (Singapore-bank proxy, his own holdings disclosed) says bank prices already price that in. Valuation caps upside that the earnings mechanism supports — net mildly positive but not stretched-add territory.
